historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved an agreement of up to $12,000 with Michael Painter and Associates, landscape architects, to design and supervise the rehabilitation of the Children's Playground in Golden Gate Park, made possible by gifts including one from an anonymous donor.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved Michael Painter and Associates' design development plan for rebuilding the Children's Playground, after approving his schematic plans in February; the general manager said Painter had been asked to keep the playground's original apparatus.
Ground was broken on May 17 for the reconstruction of the historic Children's Playground in Golden Gate Park, as the general manager reported to the Recreation and Park Commission.

Mayor George R. Moscone was to rededicate the rebuilt Children's Playground as the Mary B. Connolly Children's Playground on March 22, with Mr. and Mrs. Walter A. Haas and Mr. and Mrs. Walter Shorenstein, whose gifts began the project, and to unveil a granite marker calling it the oldest public playground in the United States; it had reopened in December.

The general manager reported the $700,000 renovation of the Children's Playground complete, paid for by a state grant and Open Space funds, with a new play area accessible to children of varying abilities, a small theater in the renovated barn, a dry stream bed and sand play.
A new site for the Children's Quarters was graded, taking about 50,000 cubic yards of fill, paid for partly by $4,000 from the street railway companies.
The children's playgrounds opened, with a merry-go-round, donkey rides, goat carts, swings, see-saws, spring-boards and maypoles.

At the Children's Quarters the ball grounds were being turned into a lawn for boys under fourteen, walks were laid out, the donkey run changed, and an asphalt rink built for roller skating and bicycles.

The children's quarters and their grounds were finished: the two-story house with a playroom below and a restaurant above, its balcony overlooking the merry-go-round, donkey and goat-cart rides, swings, see-saws, spring-boards and maypole, with a ball ground beyond; the playground paid its own way from restaurant and ride takings.
